how_it_wins:
Two commanders stand at opposite ends of one door. Brallin bills the table for every card that leaves your hand — each discard is 1 damage to EACH opponent and a +1/+1 counter. Shabraz pays you for every card that arrives — each draw is a +1/+1 counter and 1 life. A wheel is two payments, and the 99 is the pile of cards that gets paid twice.

One thing has to be true, and it is not the thing you wait for. The declaration marks exactly one group `required`: a wheel. The goldfish (10,000 games, seed 42) reads a wheel drawn in 0.991 of games, 0.943 by turn six, mean turn 1.772. What you wait for is a payoff standing at the door — both partners on the battlefield is 0.834 by turn six, mean turn 5.395. The gap between 1.772 and 5.395 is the ignition window.

The split the cards do not show. The 99 holds 17 hand-refill effects and only NINE discard, so only nine pay Brallin: Anje's Ravager, Burning Inquiry, Jace's Archivist, Khorvath's Fury, Magus of the Wheel, Queen Kayla bin-Kroog, Reforge the Soul, Tolarian Winds, Windfall. Six shuffle the hand into the library and two put it on the bottom; those eight pay the Shabraz half only, and refill the table with you. A discard wheel is drawn in 0.948 of games, 0.809 by turn six.

Two kills come off that one ignition: the wheel kill assembles in 0.867 of games and 0.530 by turn six, the air kill in 0.848 and 0.540.

Know which one pays. Summed over turns one to eight the goldfish gives 81.741 combat damage against 6.769 cumulative event damage — 92.4% against 7.6%. You win by attacking with what the draws built. Brallin's bill is the tax, not the clock.

What the table misreads: they see a draw deck and two 3/3s and rank you fourth. Stack 001 is the correction — one Windfall with both commanders out is 7 damage to each seat, 7 life to you, and two 10/10s. Say 7 per seat, never 21; 21 is the pod total.
mulligan:
Keep for the enabler, not the payoffs. You keep to a CLASS, and the class is a wheel.

All payoff and no wheel — four lands, Psychosis Crawler, Niv-Mizzet, Glint-Horn Buccaneer — is a ship. Every one of those is a blank until a hand empties.

Prefer a DISCARD wheel. Burning Inquiry ({R}), Tolarian Winds ({1}{U}), Windfall ({2}{U}) and Reforge the Soul pay Brallin. Winds of Change ({R}), Molten Psyche and Commit // Memory refill you and pay him nothing.

Lands: three. The goldfish keeps its first seven in 0.806 of games, but the diagnostic (10,000 games, seed 20260826) reads two stalled turns in a row in 0.1468 of games, [0.1400, 0.1539] — worse than any tracked deck — and 6,504 of 7,780 stalled turns were mana-short, not hand-empty. You do not run out of cards. You run out of lands.

Read the lands, not the number. There is now ONE basic, an Island, and EIGHT lands carry a basic land type: Glittering Massif, Hallowed Fountain, Irrigated Farmland, Island, Raugrin Triome, Sacred Foundry, Steam Vents, Thundering Falls. Five of the eight carry Plains and six carry Island. Floodfarm Verge gates blue on ‘a Plains or an Island’ and Riverpyre Verge on ‘an Island or a Mountain’, so the basic switches both on. Nimbus Maze does not follow: it gates WHITE on an Island and BLUE on a Plains, so the Island buys the colour you are long on and leaves the Maze making {C} for blue. With neither type down, the two Verges make W and R only and the Maze makes only colourless.

Blue is what binds — 32 land sources against a 36 target, on-curve 0.785 counting only ungated lands — and Shabraz costs {3}{W}{U}. A two-lander of Floodfarm Verge and Nimbus Maze is a one-colour hand.

combo_lines.001:
This line turns on WHEN the fourteen triggers go on the stack. The discard and the draw are one resolution of Windfall; no player receives priority inside it. So all seven Brallin triggers and all seven Shabraz triggers wait, and Brallin is a 3/3 with no counters the whole time — through the discard AND through all seven draws. Only when Windfall has finished resolving and gone to the graveyard do the fourteen go on the stack together.

What it proves: Brallin triggers once per CARD you discard, seven times for seven cards. Each trigger is 1 damage to EACH opponent, so the total is 7 per seat and 21 across the pod. It also proves the counter count: one counter per resolution, so seven resolutions make Brallin a 10/10 and Shabraz a 10/10 flier, and you gain 7.

What it does not prove: nothing about a second damage source; that is stack 004. Note which cards did nothing. Rielle and Library of Leng were in the hand being discarded, not on the battlefield, so neither functioned: no extra draw, no card kept on top. Cast the wheel with the tollbooths already down.
combo_lines.002:
This line turns on one word: whether a discard redirected somewhere other than the graveyard is still a discard. It is. Library of Leng changes where the card goes, not whether the discard happened, so all four cards still count and Brallin still triggers four times — 4 per seat, 12 across the pod.

You bill the table for the cards and you do not lose them: the four go on top of your library in an order you choose, and Windfall's draw takes them straight back.

Read the draw count carefully, because it is not your discard count. Windfall draws everyone cards equal to the GREATEST number any single player discarded. So you draw your four back plus one card from beneath them. The corollary bites the other way: when you are the player with the biggest hand, you set the number for the table, and a full grip feeds three opponents seven cards each.

What it does not prove: Shabraz is off the board in this scenario, so the draw half is unpriced here. And the Leng trick has a hole stack 003 finds.
combo_lines.003:
This line turns on the difference between a cost and an effect, and it is the hole in the Library of Leng trick. Leng reads 'if an EFFECT causes you to discard a card'. A cycling cost's discard is paid during activation — no spell or ability resolved, so there is no effect, so Leng never applies. Raugrin Triome is in the graveyard and you cannot put it back on top.

Brallin does not care. His trigger condition is just 'you discard a card', and a cost payment is a discard: he triggers, and his trigger goes on the stack ABOVE the cycling ability, so the damage resolves BEFORE you draw. One counter, 1 damage per seat, 3 across the pod, then the draw.

Cycling is your instant-speed access to Brallin when you have no wheel, and nine cards in the 99 cycle — among them Shark Typhoon, Magmakin Artillerist, Nimble Obstructionist, Decree of Silence, Ominous Seas and three of the lands. If a seat is at 1, cycle in response and they are dead before the card is drawn.

What it does not prove: Shabraz is off the board here, so whether the cycle's draw also pays her is untested.
combo_lines.004:
This line turns on per-CARD against per-EVENT. Artist's Talent at level 3 replaces each noncombat damage event your sources deal with that damage plus 2.

Brallin's seven triggers are seven separate events. Each becomes 1 + 2 = 3, so seven resolutions deal 21 to each seat. Magmakin Artillerist's is ONE trigger — 'whenever you discard one or more cards' fires once per discard event, not once per card — so its 7 becomes 7 + 2 = 9, once. Total 30 per seat, 90 across the pod, three opponents from 40 to 10 off a single seven-card wheel.

Glint-Horn Buccaneer bills per card like Brallin; Magmakin bills per wheel. They are the same card until the Talent is at level 3, and then they are not.

Two more facts from the same line. The +2 is dealt by Brallin or by Magmakin, never by Artist's Talent, which deals zero damage all line. And Brallin's counters are unaffected: one per resolution, seven, 10/10.

What it does not prove: the Talent is stipulated at level 3 from an earlier turn. Getting there is {1}{R} then {2}{R} then {2}{R}, and only the last level does this.

threat_assessment:
No games are logged. Nothing below is table experience — it is a model and one simulation, and the simulation needs reading carefully.

THE FORGE RECORD, HONESTLY. 120 games against standard-v3 returned 13 wins of 105 decided — 0.124, interval [0.074, 0.200]. The other seats: sythis-enchantress 0.505 [0.411, 0.599], abaddon 0.276 [0.200, 0.368], jarad-graveyard 0.095 [0.053, 0.166]. Marginal intervals; no difference was computed. The seat's own `engine_casts` says the engine never ran: Windfall 0 casts and 6 discards, Jace's Archivist 0 and 7. Only Burning Inquiry, at {R}, was cast — 14 times. The AI will not empty its own hand. That seat carries decklist_sha256 6a639725 — v0.1.0, which ran Wheel of Fortune, Astral Drift and Ceremonial Knife, none of them in the 99 now. No Forge figure for this deck is a verdict, and none is absent either. Every goldfish figure here is the working list; the sleeved list is v1.0.0, which predates both Shelter and the Island.

WHEN YOU STOP BEING IGNORED. Three signals. The counters: the pair carry 6.78 by turn six and 38.457 by turn ten. The second body: both are down by turn six in 0.834 of games. The second damage source: Glint-Horn Buccaneer or Magmakin Artillerist turns one wheel into two bills, and stack 004 is the number a table remembers — Magmakin and Brallin under Artist's Talent at level 3, seven discards, 30 damage to each seat, 40 to 10.

WHAT TO DO ABOUT IT. Sequence the wheel last. Put the tollbooths down on quiet turns and pay them all at once; a wheel in your graveyard is the moment the table starts reading you as a draw engine.

COUNT THEIR MANA BEFORE YOU FIRE. Assume a blue seat with three or more open holds a counter, a white seat with four holds a sweeper. KEEPING A 3/3 ON THE TABLE is four cards against a 5–7 target — Lightning Greaves, Swiftfoot Boots, Kefnet the Mindful and Shelter, the cheapest and the only one that protects a creature at instant speed by targeting it. Shelter is not the only instant-speed answer: Decree of Silence's cycling is an activated ability from your hand (702.29a) and counters target spell, at {4}{U}{U}. The goldfish prices only the two Equipment: drawn in 0.661 of games, 0.342 by turn six, tied with the second damage source at 0.343 for the thinnest of the twelve declared groups.

Know what you cannot do. deck-audit answers ZERO of five permanent classes and calls that a floor. Against a problem permanent that has resolved, this deck's answer is usually to win first.
matchups:
ENCHANTMENT VALUE / CONTROL (the Sythis shape). The pod's best seat at 0.505, and in that record it eliminated this deck 45 times against abaddon's 18 and jarad's 12. It wins long, so do not play long. The unopposed goldfish kills by turn seven in 0.631 and by turn eight in 0.888; that is your window and it closes. Smothering Tithe taxes it without asking you to interact, and your own wheel switches it on — every card the table draws is {2} or a Treasure. Rhystic Study reads their CASTS, not their draws, so a wheel does not fire it.

GRAVEYARD MIDRANGE (the Jarad shape). Your own engine works against you and the fix is picking a different wheel. Five of the nine discard wheels fill EVERY graveyard — Burning Inquiry three cards each, and Jace's Archivist, Magus of the Wheel, Reforge the Soul and Windfall a whole hand each — which is what a graveyard deck wants. The six shufflers put hands into libraries instead, and three of them — Echo of Eons, Time Reversal, Commit // Memory — shuffle GRAVEYARDS in as well. Against a graveyard deck those three are removal. They pay Brallin nothing, so you trade your damage half for their engine.

CONTROL AND COUNTERSPELLS. Exactly two cards in the 99 walk through a counter: Nezahal, Primal Tide and Niv-Mizzet, Parun both read ‘this spell can't be countered’. Nimble Obstructionist is not the answer it looks like — it counters an activated or triggered ability only, never a Swords to Plowshares and never a wrath. Decree of Silence counters a spell off its cycling for {4}{U}{U}.

GO-WIDE AND TOKEN DECKS. The worst class for the 99 as built. Zero sweepers, and the audit answers zero of the five permanent classes. Brallin's damage hits players, not creatures, so a wide board does not shrink. Race it in the air: Shabraz flies, and The Locust God, Shark Typhoon, Improbable Alliance and Drake Haven all make fliers off cards moving. The goldfish has no blockers, which is the one assumption this matchup breaks.

ANYTHING WITH A HAND-SIZE OR DRAW REPLACEMENT. Stated as an assumption, not a measurement: a seat with an opposing draw-replacement effect turns your wheel into their card advantage, and a seat with a discard tax turns it into nothing. Your own hand-size relief — Library of Leng, Reliquary Tower, Nezahal — is a three-card group drawn in 0.776 of games and 0.464 by turn six. Leng does double duty: stack 002 proves a discard redirected to the top of your library is still a discard, so it keeps the cards AND bills the table.
